summary: External cross-check of 15 EWB-masked AR tracks (Aug-Nov 2026): 10/15 confirmed by specific regional rainfall/flood events in the matching window, 4/15 supported only as regional wet anomalies (context), 1/15 none found. CONFIRMED: a3bb50cc (Patagonia storm + Río Gallegos flooding + SMN daily records, Aug 5-6); fbe99f30 (Typhoon Dolphin landfall E China Aug 9-10, Shaanxi flood evacuations Aug 6, Beijing 99.5mm Aug 7, Baguio 355mm Aug 5-7); 22039c3a (Patagonia rain/snow 'gran diluvio' Aug 13-17, SMN records 16-19/8); 806867ad (Korea stationary-front rain Aug 28-Sep 1, Yeonggwang 579.5mm, disaster HQ activated Aug 30 - only the Korean end corroborated; IMD shows no Bay of Bengal cyclone in-window); 3d32db12 (SCS Raphaela Aug 26-28, EUR 3.3bn losses, Ireland flood Aug 27-29); 82dc9c1b (KZN/Durban flooding Sep 14-15, SAWS warnings); 6ad93bd2 (Hurricane Isaias Gulf/SE US landfall Oct 9, FEMA disaster declarations); b4afeee6 (Storms Adam/Austen/Boelo-Manja, Iberia to NW Europe & N-Germany coastal flooding, Oct 18-27); 3935b8c5 (SE Qld/NE NSW multi-state storm, 8 flood warnings, 200-400mm Sunshine Coast, Oct 22-26); 43e1cd0e (West Texas record Oct 29-30 rain, Del Rio 4.58in - but the track's US Northeast end was dry in-window per DC daily history). CONTEXT only: 29d2a97a (Aug 7-8 WA cold front, 10-35mm, BOM monthly summary); 85df401a & 695a34bd (western/Bering Alaska had a record-wet August - Galena record 7.85in, St. Paul 2nd-wettest Aug ever - but no event-specific reports tied to Aug 27-Sep 5); 4a9c67b0 (BOM 8 Oct update: widespread rain reaching South Australia; no flood reports found). NONE FOUND: 06ceb4d8 (E Europe/Russia Oct 5-6) - moreover Copernicus/ERA5 October 2026 bulletin reports that exact region was DRYER than average in October, suggesting a possible detection error or a track over sparsely populated northern Russia. PHYSICAL-PLAUSIBILITY FLAGS: (1) fbe99f30's peak IVT of 2972 kg/m/s over land is world-record class (even typhoon-core ocean IVT rarely exceeds ~2000-2500 in 6-hourly ERA5); the corroborated extreme rain in-window was Typhoon Dolphin-driven, so this 'AR' is most likely a tropical-cyclone moisture flux (or a masking/unit artifact) - recommend excluding TC cores before peak-IVT statistics. (2) 6ad93bd2's 2018 kg/m/s is likewise consistent with a hurricane (Isaias) core crossing land, i.e. a likely AR/TC classification ambiguity. (3) 85df401a and 695a34bd have identical peak IVT (1126) and near-identical bounding boxes days apart - suspicious duplicate tracking of the same storm system. (4) 3d32db12 and 82dc9c1b corroborate heavy rain in-region+window but the impacts are attributed by sources to severe convective storms and a cut-off low respectively - AR co-location is plausible but mechanism attribution needs care. (5) 43e1cd0e corroborated only at the Texas end; the Great Lakes/Northeast end had no wet reports in-window. No fabricated sources: all URLs/quotes above were retrieved live on 2026-11-07.
